item.title: The Loneliness of Mad King Trump
item.description: Trump is purging MAGA of heretics, and his success will be his doom.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
By the time you read this, it is possible that Trump has attacked Cuba or Iran or both. Trump canceled his weekend golf excursion to rush back to the White House.

On Thursday, many were anticipating a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations. There was a Qatari delegation in Tehran, and the GCC, China, and Pakistan were applying diplomatic pressure. With American warships blockading Cuba, Trump’s golf partner Lindsey Graham tweeted out: “I believe the liberation of the wonderful people of Cuba from the clutches of communism is close at hand.”

Last week, the United States indicted Cuba’s 94-year old former leader Raul Castro, creating the legal justification for the American military to kidnap Castro as they had Maduro. Decapitating Cuba would remove Russian influence from the Western hemisphere, and that would be in line with the Donroe Doctrine. Trump would be the sort to prefer a quick and easy victory in Cuba over a drawn-out and uncertain round two with Iran.

item.title: China's Third Center Strategy
item.description: China has hosted Trump, and will now host Putin. As the United States and Russia become more overt enemies, China seeks to be a friend to both.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Last week, I discussed why Trump visited China:

What would a grand bargain between China and the United States look like? The United States is primarily interested in maintaining dollar hegemony, and so it needs China to purchase US treasuries. China wants access to the US market as well as the energy resources of the Western hemisphere.

The summit has ended, and we are already seeing the broad contours of this grand bargain emerging. China has agreed to buy American LNG, and China agrees with Trump that Iran should not develop a nuclear weapon, should not close the Strait of Hormuz, and should not collect tolls.

President Xi Jinping calls for “strategic stability” between China and the United States, which I interpret to mean that both should co-operate to maintain the status quo. This is a tacit acceptance of the Donroe Doctrine, and America’s supremacy over the Western Hemisphere and America’s war against Iran. China accept America’s subjugation of Venezuela and strangling of Cuba, and China hopes that America concludes its “business” in the Middle East as soon as possible.

In return, Trump seems ready to “oppose” Taiwan independence, arguing it is a distant concern in an interview with Fox News’ Bret Baier. He has yet to approve the $12 billion arms sale to Taiwan. He wants to transfer Taiwan’s semi-conductor industry to America, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (TSMC) is obliging by expanding its operations in the United States. The United States has tried to onshore manufacturing with little success, and Trump wants to lure the Chinese manufacturing base to America. There’s a rumor circulating that the Chinese plan to invest one trillion dollars in American manufacturing.

In an interview with Sean Hannity, Trump has said that he wants 500,000 Chinese to study in America, and he will allow Chinese to buy American farmland. He claims that this is to save American colleges from bankruptcy, and farmland value from declining. As I pointed out in my Substack last week and in my most recent YouTube lecture, the main reason is to distribute a portion of the $39 trillion dollar debt to the Chinese. Eventually, I believe that Beijing will allow Chinese to purchase stable-coins (digital currency backed by US treasuries), which would allow them to participate in the US economy without causing the RMB to free-fall.

item.title: The US-China Grand Bargain
item.description: How the US and China can seek a reconciliation.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Next week, American President Donald Trump will visit Beijing for two days. The last time an American President visited Beijing was when Trump visited in November 2017. That reciprocated Chinese Xi Jinping’s April 2017 state visit to the United States, where Trump’s grandchildren recited Tang Dynasty poetry for him.

Afterwards, there followed a rapid deterioration in US-China relations:

  • In January 2018, Trump accused China of stealing intellectual property, and began imposing tariffs on China. This started a trade war that became institutionalized under Biden.

  • In December 2018, Canada detained Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou because the United States requested her extradition. In response, China arrested two Canadian nationals, and accused them of spying.

  • In January 2020, the United States canceled its Peace Corps program in China.

  • In March 2020, the United States limited the number of journalists from certain Chinese state media. China retaliated by expelling journalists from the New York Times, Washington Post, and Wall Street Journal.

  • In June 2020, Trump blamed China for spreading Covid-19 to the United States, and called it the “kung-flu.”

  • In July 2020, the United States ordered China to close its Houston consulate. China retaliated by ordering the United States to close its Chengdu consulate, and Chinese netizens petitioned for the consulate to be turned into a hot pot restaurant called “Trump Hot Pot.”

In his first term, Trump’s actions against China seemed calculated to be personal. In his second term, Trump has opted for a softer approach with China, and it seems his animus is now directed at Europe and the Democrats. The two main architects of Trump’s China strategy in his first administration — deputy national security advisor Matt Pottinger and senior counsellor for trade and manufacturing Peter Navarro — are not present in his second.

There is hope that Trump will repair the damage to US-China relations that he wantonly created in his first term, and I believe that a grand bargain between the United States and China is afoot. This is counter-intuitive, as most people believe that China aims to displace Pax Americana with Pax Sinica.

This fundamentally misunderstands the nature of the Chinese political system. To put it in the bluntest terms, the United States is democratic, and maintains political stability by exploiting other populations to benefit its own. China is authoritarian, and maintains political stability by exploiting the population to benefit the political elite.

The political systems of the United States and China complement each other, and they are both status quo powers that benefit from a global economy under heavy strain. Presidents Trump and Xi are expected to meet four times this year, and we should expect these meetings to be fruitful.

item.title: God Emperor Trump
item.description: In Trump’s hapless first term, the Democrats ridiculed him as the Orange Fuhrer. Now that he is amassing unprecedented powers, Trump will have the last laugh.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Last Sunday, Trump survived the third attempted assassination on his life. Cole Allen, a thirty-one year old California teacher, booked a room at the Hilton Hotel, the same hotel in which John Hinckley attempted to assassinate Reagan. He tried to make his way to the White House Correspondents’ Dinner with multiple weapons, and was apprehended unharmed and half-naked before he could enter the ballroom where President Trump was dining alongside Vice-President JD Vance and Speaker of the House Mike Johnson. Had Allen succeeded in his mission, 92-year old Chuck Grassley would have become President of the United States.

There were multiple shots fired, though none came from the alleged assassin. Like the pro that he is, Trump smirked at the sound of the shots, which rattled his wife and the mind-reader Oz Pearlman, that night’s entertainment.

Vance was escorted quickly out of the ballroom, and Trump took his time. His good friend Dana White (who will host a UFC fight at the White House in June) said he found the chaos “awesome.” Trump spied the ballroom clearing from backstage, and even wanted the show to go on. Before the dinner, his press secretary Karoline Leavitt giddily told everyone to watch because there would be “shots fired.” Trump had refused to join the White House Correspondents’ Dinner before as President. That evening, he brought his Cabinet, including FBI Director Kash Patel (whom Allen had specifically mentioned in his manifesto as an innocent member of the Trump administration of “rapists and pedophiles”).

item.title: The Trump New Deal
item.description: The barbaric logic of Trump's imperial madness.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
The George HW Bush has arrived in the Middle East, and Centcom has in position three of the United States’ eleven aircraft carrier strike groups. Despite the ceasefire, America’s airbridge to the Middle East continues, and America has now assembled more firepower than it had before the war commenced on February 28th. China has warned its citizens to leave Iran immediately, and the last time that China issued such a warning was on February 27th. Eighteen nations have told its citizens to leave, including the United States, Germany, France, and the United Kingdom.

Perhaps peace is possible. Trump has extended the ceasefire, and has sent his envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Islamabad, where they might hopefully run into Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who will also be visiting.

Unfortunately, Trump and the Israelis have consistently used negotiations as a cover for a sneak attack, and there are three subtle signs that this war will become both protracted and global.

The United Arab Emirates has asked for a currency swap line, and the United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has told a Senate hearing that this would benefit both the UAE as well as the United States. The UAE currently has $120 billion in US treasuries, and a loan means that the UAE would not have to divest. This begs the question: The UAE is suffering the most from this war, and so why not sell US treasuries to put pressure on Trump to end this war?

From a game theory perspective, the UAE cannot afford for the United States to walk away. Dubai’s miracle was in conjuring up a mirage of a millionaire’s paradise. Since 2014, Dubai’s millionaire population has doubled to 81,000. The twenty billionaires and 237 centimillionaires who moved their wealth to Dubai are now moving it out. Only a humbled Iran can make Dubai great again. As well, a United States defeat would mean Iran could force UAE to pay reparations with a Strait of Hormuz toll.

By borrowing money from the United States, the UAE aims to incentivize the Americans to continue the fight:

  • One major reason that the United States entered World War I is that it could not afford for the Allies to lose. By 1917, American investors had bought $2.3 billion in war bonds from the Allies, and $40 million from the Germans. By borrowing heavily from the United States, the UAE hopes to become “too big to fail.”

  • Borrowing from the United States is a way for the UAE to finance this war against Iran without incurring the wrath of the Muslim world. Trump has said that he wants the GCC to pay for the war, and he cites as precedent the 1990 Persian Gulf War when Kuwait, Saudia Arabia, the UAE, Germany and Japan covered 88 percent of the war cost ($54 billion in total).

  • We can expect this war to cost trillions, and by creating the template the UAE hopes to build a “coalition of the willing” to finance this war. We can assume that Saudi Arabia, which wants the Unites States to humble Iran, is working behind the scenes to ensure the UAE gets American financing to withstand this war. Bessent wants to extend currency swap lines to all the economies that are suffering the most from this war, primarily those of the GCC and East Asia.

The second subtle sign that this war will be protracted and global is that the Indonesian Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa, speaking at a symposium, made an off-hand suggestion to impose tolls for using the Strait of Malacca: “If we split it three ways between Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, that could be quite something, right?” He had to walk this back after the immediate backlash.

Eighty percent of China’s imported crude oil traverses the Strait of Malacca, and it’s so crucial to China’s global trade that President Hu Jintao coined the phrase “Malacca Dilemma” to describe this strategic vulnerability.

It is hard to imagine that an Indonesia high official, always sensitive of the US-China rivalry, could be so careless in a public setting. Was he testing the waters on behalf of the Americans?

item.title: The US-Iran War, Round Two
item.description: Iran over-performed in the first six weeks of this war. Expect the Americans to dominate once the ceasefire ends.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
This week there was yet another brief sliver of hope that this war would come to an end. Trump said that the war could end “very soon,” and Israel entered into a ten-day ceasefire with Hezbollah. The Iranians opened the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices dropped, and someone with impeccable timing yet again made hundreds of millions shorting oil. Once the markets closed on Friday, Trump said that “we’re going to have to start dropping bombs again.” Israel broke the ceasefire in Lebanon, and Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump is signaling a long war. He has asked for a $1.5 trillion dollar budget for the Pentagon, and the young men of America will be automatically registered for the draft starting in December. The Pentagon has asked Ford and General Motors to start manufacturing drones and munitions, which suggests that America is moving towards a war-time economy.

Congress continues in its dereliction of duty. The Senate has now failed four times to pass a resolution demanding that Trump seek Congressional approval to continue the Iran war. The House of Representatives failed by a theatrical one vote to pass the same resolution. Four Republicans abstained from voting, and Thomas Massie voted in favor. This forced the Democrats to sacrifice one of their own to deny the resolution, and Jared Golden (who does not plan to seek re-election) became the scapegoat.

Iran’s Trump card was its capacity to disrupt the global economy by depriving it twenty percent of its energy and one-third of its fertilizer. In ordering a blockade of Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Trump has raised the ante. Who will blink first?

item.title: Our WTF! Years
item.description: WTF is with this ceasefire? WTF is with Melania?
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Last Tuesday the world was on the brink. Trump threatened to bomb Iran back into the “stone age” if the Strait of Hormuz remained shut. Trump had neither reason nor objective when he started this war, but with the global economy in crisis he had found both in opening the Strait of Hormuz (which, as critics satirically point out, had been closed since the 1979 Iranian Revolution).

Trump demanded that NATO go open the Strait of Hormuz because America did not need Middle East energy, while Europe did. The Europeans are too co-opted to point out that if America had not sanctioned Russian energy and had not killed Iran’s supreme leader Europe’s economy would not face ruin. Trump’s Secretary of State Marco Rubio threatened to exit NATO because it was not a reliable ally.

Still not dizzy enough? The world expected Trump to do a TACO Tuesday, and so Trump decided to surrender unconditionally. He said that he would accept Iran’s 10-point plan (which included lifting all economic sanctions, acknowledging Iran’s sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, and providing security guarantees to Iran and its regional proxies) as the framework for a permanent peace. Trump unfroze $6 billion in Iranian assets, and sent JD Vance as his emissary to Pakistan for peace talks.

As the world celebrated at the prospect of peace in our time, the Israelis launched one hundred air-strikes in Lebanon, killing over two hundred. The Iranians had agreed to open the Strait of Hormuz, but claimed they had laid naval mines, and forgotten where. It seemed both sides were trolling each other, and Iran had agreed to talks at the insistence of China, Iran’s largest customer who depended on half of its oil exports from the Middle East. Afraid that the Israelis would blow up their negotiating team, Iran sent three planes to Pakistan, with two acting as decoys.

Yesterday, Melania Trump summoned the White House press corps to announce that she had no relationship with Jeffrey Epstein (something no one was concerned about with her husband threatening to destroy human civilization), and that Epstein’s victims should be allowed to testify before Congress.

Like most people, this is the first time I’ve heard Mrs. Trump speak, and it was jarring to hear such a shrill and high-pitch voice. I remember hearing Jared Kushner speak for the first time denying the Russia-gate allegations, and found it equally jarring to hear such a shrill and high-pitch voice. The difference between the two was that Kushner was forced to respond, while Mrs. Trump volunteered for the spotlight, which was unusual for her.

item.title: World War Trump
item.description: The war to break the world, and make Trump.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
The Iranians have shot down an American F-15. Both the Americans and the Iranians are racing to find the pilot. The Iranians have damaged a Warthog as well as two Blackhawk helicopters involved in the search and rescue mission.

The stakes cannot be higher. If the Iranians capture the pilot, it will be as though they have tamed a God who had soared haughtily throwing thunderbolts. If America did not have a ground invasion plan before, it does now. Seizing Kharg Island or locating Iran’s uranium stockpiles are no longer the priority. What matters now is maintaining the illusion of America’s aerial supremacy, which Secretary of War Peter Hegseth boasted about having been achieved at the beginning of this war.

The US Air Force was not designed for a war of attrition. American airpower is designed to “shock and awe” — not “loiter over the top of Tehran” “to negotiate with bombs,” as Hegseth demanded. As this war drags on, there will be an acceleration in accidents and malfunction. To actually achieve aerial supremacy, the Americans will need to launch a ground invasion to clear Iranian air defenses. Otherwise, the Iranians will get more “lucky” in shooting down American aircrafts, and American pilots will be paraded on Iranian state television.

Is this war affecting Trump’s sleep as much as everyone else’s? Not at all. He is obsessed with turning the White House into the Mar-a-Lago of the North. He is probably more angry at a judge impeding his White House ballroom renovation than at the Iranians for defying him. Trump has even threatened to walk away — because it’s the Europeans who depend on oil from the Strait of Hormuz.

This war threatens to destroy the American empire, and collapse the global economy. Trump can sleep well at night because everything is going to plan.

item.title: Trump's Never-Ending War
item.description: America will fight this war to the bitter end, even at the cost of its soul.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
The YouTuber “HistoryLegends” has a good video analyzing the Pentagon’s options for an amphibious assault against Iran. He argues that seizing Kharg Island would be a high-risk low-reward strategy that would leave American forces vulnerable to Iranian drones and artillery. Taking Qeshm Island promises control over the Strait of Hormuz, but would demand American mission creep into the Iranian coastline. He explains that the best option would be an amphibious landing in the Chabahar Bay, an area in southern Iran where America has established aerial and naval supremacy. A Sunni minority people called the Balochs live in the area, and their extremists have been in conflict with Tehran. The Marines could establish a Forward Operating Base there, baiting the Iranians rather than become sitting ducks.

It is endearing that one can still believe that an administration that went into this war without a strategy and a purpose would suddenly develop a methodical and long-term approach. Trump’s team do not believe they are losing the war. They believe that their problems are an enemy too stupid to know they have been defeated, a domestic media that whines about how long this war is taking, and unfaithful doomsayers (such as Joe Kent and Tucker Carlson).

item.title: The US-Iran End Game
item.description: This war ends with the rise of Pax Judaica.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
We are but three weeks into this senseless and pointless war, and it seems certain now that the Americans will commit boots on the ground. The Pentagon is deploying an additional five thousand troops to the Middle East, and Netanyahu has re-appeared to say that the war must be won on the ground, not from the air. Trump has asked for two hundred billion dollars from Congress, signaling that he intends to fight a long war. (Since February 2022, the United States has provided $183 billion to Ukraine).

An empire in decline suffers from a lethal dose of hubris and desperation, and Trump seeks a knock-out punch. Trump started the war with no clear objective, and now he has decided upon an impossible objective: Control the Strait of Hormuz, and permit safe maritime navigation.

As I discussed last week, Kharg Island promises to the point of entry and escalation. With a daring assault on the island, Trump’s television brain hopes that he will regain the narrative, and stir the patriotic pride of Americans. With ninety percent of Iran’s oil exports in his very large and not small hands, Trump believes he can force Iran to negotiate a favorable peace.

As every military analyst has pointed out, it’s one thing to take Kharg Island, and quite another to hold it. The Marines will be sitting ducks, and the Iranians can besiege them with artillery. Tens of thousands of infantry will be necessary to secure the Iranian coastline, and hundreds of thousands will be necessary to hunt down Iran’s underground bases in the Zagros Mountains.

Meanwhile, the Iranians have proven that – if pushed too far – they could in one day mine the Strait of Hormuz, set ablaze the energy infrastructure of the GCC, and torpedo the global economy, which would result in revolutions, famines, and resource wars around the world. In retaliation for the Israelis bombing their natural gas field, the Iranians with one blow destroyed 17 percent of Qatar’s LNG capacity, resulting in at least $20 billion in revenue loss.

If you are a certified member of the global financial elite (which includes City of London, Wall Street, sovereign wealth funds, and the Bank of International Settlements), now might be a good time to panic. How will transnational capital respond to this Middle East quagmire?

Let us do a thought experiment. Let us pretend that this elite of central bankers, asset managers, and private bankers assemble an emergency meeting in Basel. Should they continue to prop the financial markets, the US dollar, and consumer confidence, or let them all nose-dive? Even before their private jets land, they should have all come to the same set of conclusions.

item.title: Vietnam Redux
item.description: An American occupation of Kharg Island would start another forever war. Trump may have no choice.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Two weeks into this war, and it is going as well as anyone who is outside Washington could expect. The United States and Israel continue to attempt to bomb Iran into submission, which like most aerial bombardment campaigns has hardened the resolve of the Iranian people. There have been notable successes, such as the assassination of the Ayatollah Khamenei on the first day. There have also been inexcusable tragedies, such as the bombing of a girls’ school in southern Iran that killed over 170, also on the first day.

Iran’s fast and furious response — closing the Strait of Hormuz, targeting US military assets throughout the Middle East, and pressuring the GCC economies — has surprised and shaken the Trump administration. In a major escalation, Trump has ordered the bombing of Kharg Island, and the Pentagon has ordered the deployment of at least 2,500 marines to the Middle East from Japan. There is now fear that the marines will be ordered to seize and occupy Kharg Island, which Trump believes would strangle the Iranian war economy.

item.title: The Acceleration
item.description: An American ground invasion of Iran would be a disaster. That’s the plan.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
We are only a week into this war, and Trump is already keen on a ground invasion of Iran. There are reports that American special forces are embedded with the Kurds, and the Americans and Israelis are bombarding police stations and military bases in northwest Iran to pave the way for a Kurdish invasion from Iraq. Today, there are rumors circulating that American soldiers have received their deployment orders.

Two years ago, I predicted a disastrous US ground invasion of Iran. It is not a surprise to me that the relentless air-strikes of the Americans and Israelis are neither degrading the Iranian military’s will to fight nor the population’s sense of unity. Nor is it a surprise that this war has expanded into a regional conflagration, and that Russia is providing Iran with targeting intelligence. What is surprising is the acceleration of events. There seems to be a script in place, and the actors are racing to the climax.

You would think that the Americans would want to bombard the Iranians for at least six months before committing ground troops. Experts believe that America needs at least 500,000 soldiers for a ground invasion of Iran to be feasible (I believe the number to be two million). It would take at least one year to organize such a force, and to prepare the supply networks.

This Trump administration is allergic to planning, and prefers praying. This worked out miraculously in Venezuela, less so in Iran. This is a war in search of a strategy and a purpose, and perhaps by throwing “boots on the ground” this will galvanize the public, and overnight a million young Americans will volunteer to die for God and country.

If God does not will this miracle then Trump will order a draft, and the streets of America will burn just like in the Vietnam era. Trump’s team do not seem to have a concrete plan for Iran. But they do have a detailed plan to deploy the National Guard nation-wide in case of unrest.

Trump does not have a plan to win the war. He has a plan to lose this war to save the world.

item.title: World War III Begins
item.description: This morning America launched Operation Epic Fury to decapitate the Tehran leadership. A few hours later, the entire Middle East is in flames.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
At around eight in the morning on Saturday, the Americans and Israelis bombarded Iran with missiles, aiming for the Ayatollah Khamenei and President Masoud Pezeshkian. The Israelis claimed to have killed Khamenei, but this is yet to be confirmed. Among the first confirmed casualties in this war are 51 girls when their elementary school in southern Iran was bombed.

In a video speech, President Trump announced that America was intent on overthrowing the Iranian government, which he blamed for sponsoring terrorism and suppressing the Iranian people. He encouraged the Revolutionary Guard Corps to surrender, and the Iranian people to rise up. He warned that there would be American casualties.

As promised, Iran retaliated by setting the whole region on fire. Its missiles targeted Israel, as well as the GCC countries of Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, and Bahrain. The Houthis have joined the battle, and closed off the Red Sea to shipping. America is bombing the Shia militias in Iraq, and Israel is bombing Hezbollah in Lebanon.

American officials have stated that Operation Epic Fury will be a four-day operation, which means that it should end on Tuesday March 3rd. That coincides with the Jewish holiday of Purim when Israel celebrates how Jews rallied together to foil an extermination plot in ancient Persia, and killed 75,000 of their enemies (as recounted in the Book of Esther). That day is also when a Blood Moon will appear. Freemasons (who control America’s national security apparatus) revere the number “33.”

item.title: Countdown to Iran
item.description: An American strike on Iran would launch World War Three. That's the plan, at least.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
America has positioned one-third of its naval assets into the Middle East, and the super-carrier Gerald Ford has crossed the Strait of Gibraltar en route to the Arabian Sea. Not since Operation Iraqi Freedom in 2003 has America assembled such “maximum lethality” – which suggests that the Americans are more interested in regime change than in negotiating leverage. On Polymarket, the odds of an American air strike before March 15th stand at fifty percent.

Round two will be different from last June’s 12-Day War, in which the Iranians and Americans choreographed a conflict. Diplomacy still has a chance, but the American demand that Iran abandons its ballistic missiles programs without sanctions relief is designed to be insulting. It is ominous that Trump’s envoys are Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, two Zionists close to Netanyahu.

When Trump assembled an armada against Venezuela, Maduro danced for peace. Now that it’s Iran’s turn, the Ayatollah Khamenei tweets for war, and threatens to sink American carriers. The Iranians partially closed the Strait of Hormuz for a few hours, signaling their intention to blockade the global economy. They also burned statues of Baal, broadcasting their belief that theirs is a war against the Great Satan.

It seems that the Iranian regime is on the precipice. Decades of sanctions have made Iran corrupt, fractured, and vulnerable. In January 2020, the Americans assassinated Qasem Soleimani without consequence. October 7th surprised the Iranians more than the Israelis, and they were powerless to help their proxies. The fall of the Assad regime in Syria opened up an air corridor for Israel to bomb Iran with impunity. In the 12-Day War, Israel assassinated many high-level Iranian officials and scientists, revealing the depth of Mossad penetration into the highest echelons of power. Last month, protests roared across Iran, and security forces killed thousands. Given how easily Delta Force swooped in to abduct Maduro on January 3rd, what fighting chance does the Ayatollah have?

item.title: Welcome to the Rupture
item.description: We are living in the midst of World War Three, an epic battle between an old order refusing to die, and a new order struggling to be born.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
Everyone feels that 2026 is an acceleration – but of what? Decades have passed in weeks. How to explain the traumatic release of the Epstein files, the kidnapping of Maduro, the countdown to war in Iran, the sudden rise and collapse of gold and silver and bitcoin, Trump’s aggression towards Greenland and Canada, and ICE thuggery in Minnesota? With earthquakes everywhere, let us examine how and why the geo-political tectonic plates are shifting.

A vital clue is the proliferation of the occult term “New World Order.” Mark Carney, central banker and occultist, bandied the term in Beijing, and JD Vance, MAGA prince and occultist, did as well in an interview with Megyn Kelly. They are political nemeses, and in referencing the same occult code they offer competing visions of the future. In his viral World Economic Forum speech, Carney calls our time “the rupture,” and future historians will call it “World War Three.” Writing a century before, the Italian Marxist Antonio Gramsci described our world the best:

“The old world is dying, and the new world struggles to be born: now is the time of monsters.”

Let me summarize the occult understanding of the world, and how it applies to geo-politics. Schools teach matter creates mind, but secret societies teach the opposite. As Immanuel Kant taught us and which neuroscientists have confirmed, we hallucinate our reality. Mystics teach that reality are vibrations that we manifest into the visible, and this is a truth that quantum physicists have confirmed. True wealth is our imagination, and as Plato illustrated with his “allegory of the cave” the powers-that-be create reality itself by manipulating and focusing our attention. The private banking cartel of the Anglo-American empire (as championed by Mark Carney) manufactured the most powerful tool to focus our attention, but this old monetary order is dying because of rising inequality, reoccurring financial scandals, and endless money printing. This money culture has also made us lonely, depressed, and alienated.

A new technological order struggles to be born, and the tech oligarchs have chosen Trump and Vance to usher in an AI surveillance state. If money can no longer capture our imagination, then AI will by imprisoning us in our individual Matrix. Think the book Brave New World meets the movie “Her.” A technocratic elite will manage our world, while we’re all devoted to our AI lover or demon or alien or whatever inner hell we choose. We can now understand why Sam Altman is confident in asking for 1.4 trillion dollars for new data centers from investors when OpenAI only generated about twelve billion dollars in revenues last year. When AI scientists say that AI will soon achieve human sentience, what they really mean is that soon the human imagination will become digitized (which is happening in China right now). With the advent of digital ID and currency and with AI surveillance and omnipresence (in China, our mobile phones are own Communist political commissars), human thought processes change from one that is intuitive and imaginative to one that is material and mechanical, thus killing the spirit and soul of society. But at least we’ll no longer be lonely or depressed or alienated – we’ll all be happy robots.

item.title: Twilight of the Liberal Elite
item.description: The Epstein files are a political earthquake that will shatter all illusions.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
I need to apologize. In my last post, I referenced an e-mail in which Jeffrey Epstein told Elon Musk to go away. It turns out that the e-mail was a hoax, and I should have been more vigilant. I wanted it to be true because it would have been too funny (especially because of Elon’s viral tweet that Trump was in the Epstein files). As well, the tone and substance of the e-mail thread was indistinguishable from authentic ones, which together reveal the elite as giddy and careless teenagers.

With this recent release of three million documents, Trump’s Department of Justice claims that over half have been released, and that there will be no indictments and no further release – which has convinced many that as damning as the released redacted documents are, the remaining ones may topple the edifice of power in America. There’s already fall-out across the Atlantic: Keir Starmer may have to resign because of his faith in Peter Mandelson, a close Epstein associate.

That Epstein involved himself with the rich and famous, in geo-politics and high finance suggest that at the heart of global power is a criminal network engaged in money-laundering, arms-dealing, and human-trafficking.

The e-mails suggest that what permits trust, secrecy, and co-ordination among this transnational elite is Satanic pedophilia. In a text exchange, urologist Harry Fish prescribed to Epstein some medicine to correct his erectile dysfunction, which would then allow them to get “pizza and grape soda.” Someone else e-mailed Epstein, and suggested “lets go for pizza and grape soda again.” As Tucker Carlson asked, why did Epstein (who was so obsessed with health and fitness that he became friends with longevity guru Peter Attia) have such a preference for peasant food?

item.title: The Great Unraveling
item.description: The Democrats are so clueless I have to wonder if they're in on the plan.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
This past week, silver hit a historic high of $120 and gold $5600, and with the dollar weakening the sky was the limits. Yesterday, in a flash, the many lost everything (about ten trillion in market value) to the few. Those who over-leveraged to go long on metals were the losers, and those who shorted were the winners.

It is safe to assume that the winners were the oligarchs. The odds of silver crashing thirty percent were astronomically low, and those who tried to buy on the dip were prevented by “technical errors.”

This recalls the January 2021 GameStop scandal, in which hedge funds such as Citadel put a short squeeze on the retail outlet. Retail investors rallied to GameStop’s defense, and the online brokerage Robinhood halted trading to prevent the surging stock from liquidating the short squeezes. It was later revealed that Robinhood generated forty percent of its revenue by selling trade details from retail investors to Citadel before executing the trades. This reeked of insider trading and conspiracy, but the class action lawsuits, Congressional hearings, and SEC investigations eventually fizzled out.

The game is rigged, and the house always wins.

item.title: Carney's Speech and Trump's Letter
item.description: Mark Carney rallies the faithful at Davos to sell out Canada.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
In this year’s meeting of the global elite in Davos, Switzerland, the Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney received a standing ovation. He is only the third man to have received such a distinction from such a somber audience (the other two were Nelson Mandela and Volodymyr Zelenskyy). His speech would have won a freshman composition award at Harvard or Oxford, and Carney had studied at both.

Carney invoked two allusions. The first was to Thucydides, whose The Peloponnesian War illustrated how the Athenian empire cannibalized its allies. Carney implored the world to stand together against such mafia imperialism. “If you’re not at the table, you’re on the menu” were his memorable choice of words.

item.title: Iran, Greenland, and Canada
item.description: The world this week: Trump calls off Iran War, Trump and Europe prepare for war in Greenland, and Carney visits Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Predictive History
item.content:encoded:
I am experimenting with a new format this week. I will examine three major geo-political events of the past week, and provide analysis and context.

Let’s start with Iran. Many expected America to strike Iran, but Trump canceled airstrikes. There’s reporting that Qatar, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia talked Trump out of bombing Iran because they were afraid of regional instability. To maintain the narrative that Israel is in charge, Netanyahu claimed that he asked Trump to call off the strikes. What happened?
